# Damage over Time never critically strikes

- **Status:** ✅ Confirmed
- **Skills affected:** Mind Control
- **Mechanic tags:** dot, crit
- **Last verified:** 2026-07-10 by Tyra

## Setup

SS12. Mind Control, skill level 16, no gear, vs the standard Level-85 dummy — see [training-dummy](training-dummy.md). Support: Control Spell (`-100% Critical Strike Rating for the supported skill`, `+28% additional damage for the supported skill`, Lv16 interpolated to +35.5%).

## Raw data points

Mind Control (a pure skill-DoT with no hit component) went from 150 → 210.5 meter DPS with Control Spell attached — a raise, not a drop. A crit-dependent skill stripped of −100% Critical Strike Rating would have LOST its crit-damage contribution and dropped in DPS; instead the observed change matches the Control Spell's `+35.5%` additional-damage line alone (`155.4 (baseline model) × 1.355 = 210.6`, vs meter 210.5).

## Derived / confirmed formula

A DoT stage skips `crit_factor` and `double_dmg_factor` entirely — both are pinned at their no-crit/no-double-damage identity value (1.0) regardless of the source's Critical Strike Rating or Double Damage chance.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

Corroborates the Help DB's explicit statement rather than discovering something new — this in-game measurement is confirmation, not the primary source. Isolating power comes from Mind Control having zero hit component: any DPS change on it can only be attributed to the DoT mechanic, not a hit-damage side effect of the support.

## Implementation (engine model)

**Engine consequence:** a DoT damage stage must not multiply by `crit_factor` or `double_dmg_factor` — see the `DamageRow` docstring in `backend/engine/offense.py` (~L709-712), which already states this and cites this exact in-game corroboration (the Control Spell −100%-crit-but-raised-DPS result) as the reasoning.
